analysis.investment_thesis: Fabtech trades at P/E 27.6 and P/B ~2.84 (270 Cr / 95 Cr equity), both well above my strict limits, offering no margin of safety. While earnings have been positive every year since 2020, this is a recently listed small-cap with IPO-inflated pricing — precisely the setup where Mr. Market favors the seller, not the buyer.
key_strengths: Positive net profit every year 2020–2025 (5/5), growing at 26.6% CAGR to ₹13 Cr
Low leverage: borrowings ₹10 Cr vs equity ₹95 Cr (D/E ~0.10), interest cover ~17x
Promoter holding 68.49% signals skin-in-the-game; ROCE 21.2% is respectable
key_risks: P/E 27.6 and P/B ~2.84 violate Graham thresholds (<15 and <1.5) — no margin of safety
Operating cash flow ₹3 Cr vs net profit ₹13 Cr in FY25 — earnings quality concern
Micro-cap (₹270 Cr) and recent IPO; equity jumped from 52→95 Cr in FY25 (dilution via primary issue)
red_flags: FY25 OCF (₹3 Cr) is only ~23% of reported net profit — working capital leakage
Recently listed IPO: no seasoned trading history; investment bank priced to maximize seller's proceeds
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a strict Graham lens, Fabtech fails the two cardinal valuation tests. The Graham Number ceiling ≈ √(22.5 × EPS × BVPS). With net profit ₹13 Cr and equity ₹95 Cr on ~1 Cr shares (implied from ₹270 Cr cap at ₹268), EPS ≈ ₹13 and BVPS ≈ ₹94, giving a Graham Number of ~₹165 — the stock trades 62% above this intrinsic ceiling. P/E 27.6 is nearly double my <15 threshold, and P/B ~2.84 is almost twice the 1.5 limit. The balance sheet is genuinely clean (D/E 0.10, zero CWIP, reserves ₹83 Cr), and earnings have been uninterrupted — these are the bright spots. But balance-sheet strength alone cannot rescue a valuation this rich.

The cash-flow picture troubles me more than the headline numbers suggest. Despite FY25 net profit of ₹13 Cr, operating cash flow was only ₹3 Cr — this is the fourth consecutive year OCF has lagged reported earnings, consistent with stretched receivables in a turnkey engineering business where customer milestone payments are lumpy. The ₹24 Cr financing inflow and ₹26 Cr investing outflow in FY25 confirm this is fresh IPO capital being deployed, meaning current earnings power has not yet been demonstrated on the enlarged equity base. Combined with micro-cap size and the inherent information asymmetry of any recent listing, this is a speculation, not an investment. I would revisit only if the price fell below book value (~₹94) with at least three more years of OCF-backed earnings on the record.
